correctness.rationale: The four-side boundary integral gives Eα(t)/4=∫_0^1(t²+y²)^(−α/2)dy+∫_0^t(1+x²)^(−α/2)dx. Differentiation and y=t tan u yield Eα′(t)=4(1+t²)^(−α/2)(1−Hα(t)), where Hα(t)=α cos(θ)^−α ∫_0^θ cos(u)^α du with θ=atan(1/t). Its angular derivative α+α tanθ H is strictly positive, so H decreases strictly with t; H→∞ at t↓0 and Hα(1)<H1(1)=1 for α<1. This proves a unique strict global interior minimizer, including the multiplicity-two segment limit 4/(1−α). The same angular integral is strictly increasing in α, giving analytic strictly increasing tα. At α↓0, Beta/Gamma expansion log Cα=log(π/2)−α log2+O(α²) yields tα=0.5(πα/2)^(1/α)(1+O(α)); at α↑1, implicit derivative yields √2 artanh(1/√2). Independently solved root by 260-step high-precision bisection for α=.1,.3,.5,.75,.9,.99: .5 gives 0.310152114794695595035; computed upper slope 1.246450480280461026788. These numerical checks corroborate, but the derivative and asymptotic proof establishes universality.

Unique global optimum is only within centered axis-aligned rectangles and integrable singular powers α∈(0,1).

value.rationale: A complete exact optimizer classification for the natural family of centered rectangles under a fixed longest-side constraint exhibits strict interiority for every singular exponent and a non-power-law essential-singularity transition at α=0. This is a motivated shape-optimization boundary beyond routine monotonicity or isolated numerical minimization, and contrasts with previously published needle regimes under distinct constraints.
residual_risks: Not a convex-body-wide extremal theorem; the geometric class and normalization must remain explicit.
